title: Sixgun: Western Sound Effects
shortText: 145 western sound effects: three period guns in three places, horses, saloon, dynamite, shootout loops. WAV + OGG.
html:
A western town in sound: three period guns in three places, and the frontier around them

145 western sound effects: a six-shooter, a lever rifle and a scattergun as a game fires them, every gun on main street, in the saloon and in a canyon, gunfire at four distances, a shootout you turn up a tier at a time, horses at four gaits, the saloon, spurs, the wagon, the jail, the bank, dynamite, a crank gun, the desert and 28 seamless loops.

Licence, up front

Royalty free. Commercial use. No credit required. No revenue limit, no unit cap, no second licence to buy later if your game does well. Use it in as many projects as you like, on any platform. The one thing you may not do is resell the sounds themselves as sounds. The full plain language terms ship as LICENSE.txt, with a copy paste credit line if you want one.

Everything is synthesised from code. No recordings, no sample libraries, no third party clips, so there is no upstream licence behind this one and nobody can content ID claim these sounds against your project.

Hear it first

There is a free demo on this page: 29 sounds copied unaltered from the paid files. The six-shooter in all three places, the rifle at all four distances, the three shootout tiers to stack yourself, the dynamite's whole lifecycle and a gallop on dirt and on boards.

What is in it

  • Six-shooter (15)
  • Lever rifle (8)
  • Scattergun (8)
  • Three places (9)
  • Distant gunfire (7)
  • Ricochets and hits (13)
  • Saloon (14)
  • Boots and spurs (10)
  • Horses (12)
  • Wagon and trail (10)
  • Town (18)
  • Dynamite and the crank gun (9)
  • The desert (6)
  • Places (6)

Every gun in every place

The same shot sounds different on main street (it slaps back off the false fronts and flutters between them), in the saloon (a small dark pine box that swallows it) and in a canyon (the walls answer for seconds). Each of the three guns ships in all three. 9 place pairs and 9 gun pairs measured apart on the shipped files, 0 too close. The dry, close takes ship too, for your own reverb.

Distance, gait and the shootout

One rifle shot heard from four distances, each darker than the last, so you can pick the file by how far away the shooter is. Hooves at a walk, trot, canter and gallop, on dirt and on boards, as seamless loops that strike harder at each gait (9 steps measured, 0 failing). And a shootout as three loops of one length: far off, across town, in the street. Fade a tier in per intensity; every one of the 3 stacks is re-summed from the shipped files and wraps cleanly.

Four lifecycles

Dynamite, Crank gun, Wagon, Bank safe: each ships its start, a seamless loop while it runs, its stop and the way it fails (the fuse sputters out, the gun jams, a wheel breaks, the safe will not open). 16 states, every loop flag read out of the file.

Already own our other packs?

Where Sixgun fills a role Pithead, Leeward, Escapement, Unseen or Squall already fills (dynamite, keys, a struck bell, an anvil, coins, a breaking bottle, a dry desert wind), the two were measured against each other from both packs' files: 15 shared roles, every one a different sound.

Fit

  • WAV and OGG for every file, 16 bit, 44.1 kHz, mono, with a manifest listing every file by slot.
  • 28 seamless loops with sample accurate loop points in the WAV and the OGG. Checked in a blank Godot 4 project: the WAV

loops import looping with default settings.

  • One loudness band: the inner 80 percent of the pack sits inside 1.77 dB, gunshots included.
  • pack_proof.json ships with the pack: 1345 checks, 0 failed.
  • No voices and nothing musical, so it sits under any score and any cast.

Honest limits

These are synthesised sounds, not recordings of real firearms, and there are no horse or human voices. The measurements above are signal measurements, not a claim that it sounds good. That is what the free demo is for.

AI disclosure, stated truthfully: the code that generates these sounds was written with AI assistance. The sounds themselves are self contained procedural synthesis, with no generative audio model at any point. The cover art and store graphics are AI generated.

More from the same studio

  • Iron Road: Steam Railway, the period's railway: a locomotive at six speeds, a carriage, a station and a signal box.
  • Pithead: The Working Mine, the frontier's mine in three rooms, with its own blasting.
  • Squall: Weather Systems, rain, wind, blizzard and sandstorm as layers you drive with one value.
  • Verdant 55: Frontier, a Wild West tileset from the same studio: boomtown, prairie and canyon to build this town in.
